prompt.context: Your client is FlashPro Inc., a San Francisco based technology company that develops and sells wearable and mountable action cameras. FlashPro's CEO believes that the company's growth has stagnated and has hired your firm to remedy that issue.
prompt.question: The CEO has hired your firm to identify ways to remedy the growth stagnation. How would you approach this problem?

clarifying_info.q: Is the company public or private?
Where does FlashPro sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: It sells products in the US and internationally.
Their main product is CamPro, a mounted camera mainly used when playing action sports. It has also recently started being used in other recreational activities.
FlashPro does not manufacture its products; it contracts with manufacturers in China.
FlashPro sells through 3 channels: Distributors, Retail, and FlashPro's Website.
The industry is highly competitive and customers are very loyal to each brand.
Gross margin has remained steady at 50%.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Potential Market in the US
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the US action camera addressable market size in number of customers (in thousands) from 2014 through projected 2020.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Market Penetration in the U.S.
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of the US action camera potential market that has been penetrated from 2014 through projected 2020.

exhibits.title: 2016 Action Camera Market Share Distribution
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing market share among action camera competitors. Note: market share distribution is the same in the US and worldwide and has remained steady for the last 5 years. FlashPro is the only company offering wearables.

exhibits.title: New Market Entry Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table comparing four potential new country markets across current camera market size, FlashPro's expected Year 1 market share, expected annual growth over the next 3 years, and sales channel distribution (Distributors, Retail, FlashPro's Website). Dollar amounts in thousands.

data.note: After Year 3, expected market annual growth for all countries is 5%

framework: Market Analysis: assess competitors, customers, substitutes, and suppliers (5-forces style)
Profitability Tree: break down revenue (price x volume) and costs (COGS, R&D, G&A, Sales & Marketing)
Current Growth Constraints: evaluate US market saturation and market share dynamics
Revenue Growth Levers: Marketing Mix (4Ps), new geographies, product line expansion, organic vs. inorganic growth

questions.prompt: Question 1: What is FlashPro's expected Gross Profit for 2018? (Use Exhibits 1, 2, and 3)
questions.guidance: Candidate should build up from addressable market to US revenue, then scale to international, then apply gross margin. Key given data: camera price = $250, gross margin = 50%, US share = 60% of total sales, international = 40%.

math.setup: US Camera Sales = Addressable Market x Penetration Rate x FlashPro Market Share x Price; International Sales scaled by US/International split; COGS = 50% of Total Revenue; Gross Profit = Revenue - COGS. All amounts in thousands.
steps: US Camera Sales = 16,000 (2018E addressable market) x 85% (2018E penetration) x 30% (FlashPro market share) x $250 = $1,020,000 (thousands)

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are FlashPro's revenue growth prospects keeping everything constant, and what alternatives could boost their top line?
questions.guidance: Candidate should cite Exhibits 1-3 to identify that US market growth is slowing (market nearly saturated by 2020) and competition is fierce (FlashPro has held 30% share for 5 years but cannot easily take share). Strong candidates organize growth options into a framework. An excellent candidate covers: Marketing Mix (4Ps) - product attributes, sales channels, pricing, advertising; New Markets - new geographies, product line expansion; Organic (developed in-house) vs. Inorganic (M&A) approaches.

questions.prompt: Question 3: From an economic perspective, which country is most attractive to enter, and what should FlashPro consider before entering? (Use Exhibit 4)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate expected Year 3 revenue for each country and compare. An excellent candidate notes that sales channel mix matters for margins (website channel has no intermediary = higher margin; distributor/retail channels have lower margins). Best answer is Argentina because it yields the highest Year 3 revenue AND has 50% website channel (highest margin mix). Candidate should also list structured entry considerations.

math.setup: Year 1 Revenue = Current Market Size x Expected Year 1 Market Share; then apply annual growth rate for Years 2 and 3. All amounts in thousands.
steps: Japan Year 1 = $3,500 x 25% = $875; Year 2 = $875 x 1.05 = $918.75; Year 3 = $918.75 x 1.05 = $964.7 ~ $965 (casebook states ~$1,013 — growth applied to full market then share applied, or rounding difference)
Australia Year 1 = $3,500 x 20% = $700; Year 2 = $700 x 1.10 = $770; Year 3 = $770 x 1.10 = $847 (casebook states ~$932)
Casebook reference answers: Argentina $1,165, Japan $1,013, Australia $932, Sweden $951 (growth may be applied to the total market each year, then market share applied to get FlashPro revenue)
math.answer: Argentina is the most attractive: highest Year 3 revenue (~$1,165 thousand) and 50% website channel (no intermediary = highest margin)

brainstorming.prompt: What are all the different ways FlashPro could grow its top line?

categories.name: Marketing Mix (4Ps)
ideas: Product: expand product features, introduce new wearable/mountable form factors, target new activity segments (e.g., cycling, diving, gaming)
Price: tiered pricing, bundle deals, subscription accessories
Place/Channels: expand direct-to-consumer website, enter new retail partnerships, optimize distributor relationships
Promotion: increase brand advertising, influencer marketing, sponsorships with action sports athletes

categories.name: New Geographies
ideas: Enter high-growth international markets (e.g., Argentina, emerging markets)
Tailor product positioning to local consumer habits
Partner with local distributors for faster market entry

categories.name: Product Line Expansion
ideas: Launch accessories (mounts, cases, batteries, editing software)
Develop a software/subscription platform (cloud storage, editing tools)
Introduce a premium or budget camera tier

categories.name: Inorganic Growth (M&A)
ideas: Acquire a competitor to gain market share
Acquire a software company to enhance ecosystem
Partner or joint venture with a local brand in a new geography

categories.name: Organic Growth (Internal Development)
ideas: Invest in R&D for next-generation wearable technology
Develop proprietary manufacturing capabilities to reduce COGS
Build out e-commerce and direct sales infrastructure

recommendation: FlashPro should pursue a geographic expansion strategy to achieve growth, given the slowing and nearly saturated US market and fierce competition that prevents meaningful market share gains domestically

Argentina is the most attractive entry market: it offers the highest expected Year 3 revenue, a 50% direct website channel (highest margin, no intermediary), and strong market share assumptions at 35% in Year 1
risks: Entry costs (marketing, logistics, regulatory compliance, local partnerships) were not factored into the revenue analysis
Year 1 market share assumptions (especially Argentina at 35%) may be aggressive and difficult to achieve given brand loyalty dynamics in new markets
Competitive responses from local incumbents or global competitors could erode projected market share
Currency and geopolitical risk in Argentina (macroeconomic volatility)
next_steps: Conduct deeper due diligence on the Argentinian market: local competition, customer habits, regulatory environment, and economic/geopolitical conditions
Assess internal capabilities required for geographic expansion: logistics, local marketing, website localization, distribution partnerships
Develop a go-to-market plan including advertising, pricing strategy, sales channel setup, and promotional approach for Argentina
Model full P&L including entry costs and ongoing operating costs to validate profitability of expansion
